title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text:
Internal document. Tallgrass Home Care is a fictional agency used for practice data.

Last updated: January 2026

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text:
Your schedule is published every Thursday for the following week. Check it in the mobile app before your first shift.

If you cannot work a shift, call the scheduling line at 555-0142 at least 4 hours before the shift starts. A text message to your supervisor does not count as notice.

More than 3 unexcused call-outs in a rolling 90-day period results in a written warning. A second written warning within 12 months leads to a meeting with the Care Manager.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text:
Clock in with the mobile app when you arrive at the client's home. You must clock in within 7 minutes of the scheduled start time. The app checks your location, and you must be within 150 meters of the client's address for the clock-in to be accepted.

If you forget to clock out, tell your supervisor the same day. A missed clock-out must be corrected by a supervisor within 24 hours, or the visit cannot be billed.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
section: Clocking in and out > Visit notes
text: Complete your visit notes before you leave the home whenever possible. Notes must be submitted no later than 2 hours after the visit ends. Write what you did and what you observed. Do not write opinions about the client or the family.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text: The workweek runs from Sunday to Saturday. Hours over 40 in one workweek are paid at 1.5 times your regular rate. All overtime needs approval from the Care Manager before you work it.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text: Driving between client homes during the day is reimbursed at $0.67 per mile. The drive from your own home to your first client, and from your last client back home, is not reimbursed. Submit your mileage log by the 5th of the following month.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text: You earn 1 hour of paid time off for every 30 hours worked. Your balance is capped at 80 hours. Ask for time off at least 14 days in advance so that your clients can be covered.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text: Caregivers may remind a client to take medication and may open a container if the client asks. Caregivers may not administer medication, and may not decide a dose. Only a registered nurse may fill a weekly pill organizer.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
section: Care rules > Falls and other incidents
text: If a client falls, call the on-call nurse right away, even if the client says they are fine. Do not lift a client who has fallen unless they are in immediate danger. A written incident report is due within 24 hours.

title: Tallgrass Home Care - Caregiver Handbook
text: New caregivers complete an 8-hour orientation before their first solo visit. Every caregiver must complete 12 hours of in-service training each calendar year. Hours from approved workshops count toward this total.

title: Snow day policy for this winter
section: Snow day policy for this winter
text:
TALLGRASS HOME CARE MEMO

To: All caregivers and schedulers
From: Marcus Oyelaran, Operations Director
Date: November 3, 2025

Re: Snow day policy for this winter

When the office declares a Level 1 snow day, all visits go ahead as planned. Leave early and drive slowly.

When the office declares a Level 2 snow day, visits for clients on the essential list still go ahead. All other visits are cancelled. If your visit is cancelled, you are paid 2 hours of show-up pay for that visit.

The office posts the snow day level in the app by 5:30 a.m. If you are not sure, call the snow line at 555-0177.

(Fictional agency. Practice data.)

title: The Tallgrass Caregiver - Spring 2026
text: Staff newsletter - Spring 2026 - Tallgrass Home Care (fictional agency, practice data)

title: The Tallgrass Caregiver - Spring 2026
section: New clock-in app starts in March
text:
Paper timesheets are going away. The new VisitTrack app replaces them for every caregiver, and it goes live on Monday, March 9. You will use it to clock in, clock out, and write your visit notes.

We know a change like this takes time. Paper timesheets will still be accepted through Friday, March 27, which gives everyone a three-week grace period. After that date, payroll can only pay hours that are in the app.

Hands-on practice sessions are held at the Cedar Street office every Tuesday at 9:00 a.m. and every Thursday at 5:30 p.m. during February. Each session lasts about 45 minutes. Bring your own phone.

If the app will not install on your phone, call Dana Whitlock in the office at extension 214. The office has six loaner phones for caregivers who need one.

title: The Tallgrass Caregiver - Spring 2026
text: Congratulations to Rosa Delgado, our Caregiver of the Quarter. Rosa has been with Tallgrass for six years and works mostly overnight shifts. Three families wrote in to thank her this winter, and one sent a photo album. She receives a $250 gift card and a reserved parking spot for the next three months.

title: The Tallgrass Caregiver - Spring 2026
text: CPR recertification will be held on Tuesday, April 14 at the Cedar Street office. The dementia care workshop is on Wednesday, May 6 and counts for 3 in-service hours toward your yearly total.

title: The Tallgrass Caregiver - Spring 2026
text: Know someone who would make a great caregiver? The referral bonus has doubled, from $150 to $300. It is paid after the new hire completes 90 days of work. Ask the front desk for a referral card.

title: The Tallgrass Caregiver - Spring 2026
text: Questions about this newsletter? Ask at the front desk.
